explanation: printf format specifiers control column width: %-12s pads a string on the RIGHT to 12 characters (left justified) while %6d pads a number on the LEFT to 6 characters (right justified), which is what lines decimal points up. %n emits the platform line separator, so it is safer than writing a literal newline. Because every row uses the same widths, the columns line up no matter how long the individual values are -- and a value wider than its column simply pushes the line out rather than being cut off.
hints: The header uses %6s rather than %6d because SCORE is text, not a number.
